body_text:
The Nested Interval Theorem (Cantor's Intersection Theorem). Let
$I_1 \supseteq I_2 \supseteq I_3 \supseteq \cdots$ be a decreasing
sequence of non-empty closed bounded intervals
$I_n = [a_n, b_n] \subset \mathbb{R}$. Then their intersection is
non-empty: $$ \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty I_n \neq \emptyset. $$ If
furthermore the lengths satisfy
$\lim_{n \to \infty} (b_n - a_n) = 0$, then the intersection
contains precisely one point $\xi \in \mathbb{R}$.

*Proof*: Since $I_{n+1} \subseteq I_n$, the sequence of left
endpoints $(a_n)$ is non-decreasing, and the sequence of right
endpoints $(b_n)$ is non-increasing, with $a_n \leq b_m$ for all
$n, m$. The set $A = \{a_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is nonempty and
bounded above by each $b_m$. By completeness, $\xi = \sup(A)$
exists. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $a_n \leq \xi$. Moreover,
since each $b_n$ is an upper bound for $A$, $\xi \leq b_n$. Thus
$a_n \leq \xi \leq b_n$ for all $n$, meaning
$\xi \in [a_n, b_n] = I_n$ for all $n$. Hence
$\xi \in \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty I_n$. If $\lim (b_n - a_n) = 0$, any
two points $\xi_1, \xi_2 \in \bigcap I_n$ satisfy
$|\xi_1 - \xi_2| \leq b_n - a_n \to 0$, forcing $\xi_1 = \xi_2$.
